messages:
ada: Drafted a migration note for users moving from prefix-caching to the new prefetch_kv API. It's in the PR but needs examples for TS and Go and a short 'how it helps' blurb. Who can pick up the language edits?
ben: I can do the Go example. quick Q: should we demonstrate prefetching multiple keys vs a single key?
ada: single key is fine for the short guide, but add a sentence about multi-key strategies. Keep examples minimal.
carla: I'll handle the TS snippet and the prose polish. Also add a one-liner about race conditions when doing prefetch + concurrent writes to the same cache_key.
docs-bot: New PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4683  branch: optkit/prefetch-migration  author: ada (draft).
ad a: typo (ada): updated link in PR description.
jia: Small runtime callout: q5_1 on older GPUs may trigger a slower kernel at seq > 2k; recommend trying q4_0 for lower mem but mention quality tradeoff.
maya: For the perf numbers, we ran a smoke test: on dev V100, batch 4, seq512 -> 2.8x vs batch1; seq2048 -> 1.9x. Add those as example-only.
ryan: I'm adding a tiny ASCII diagram showing flow: user prompt -> prefetch at upload time -> runtime KV warm -> fast generate.
carla: Checklist I'm adding in PR comment: 
- [ ] add TS SDK snippet
- [ ] add Go SDK snippet (ben)
- [ ] add hosted API curl example
- [ ] prose: when-to-use + race-condition note + perf caveats
- [ ] CI link-check passing (console path fix if needed)

ben: Go snippet drafted, putting it in examples/go/prefetch.go in the PR. Quick version:
```go
package main
import (
  "fmt"
  "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk"
)
func main(){
  client := redwood.NewClient("$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
  model := client.Model("redwood/long-context-4k", redwood.QuantProfile("q5_1"))
  // warm KV cache
  err := model.PrefetchKV("welcome_v2", "System: You are a helpful assistant.\\n")
  if err != nil { fmt.Println("prefetch failed:", err); return }
  out, _ := model.Generate("User: please summarize...", redwood.BatchSize(2))
  fmt.Println(out.Text)
}
```

ada: thanks ben. I'll trim the Go example for length and add link to the full example repo.
carla: TS snippet done and added a curl example for hosted customers. Note: our hosted endpoint for prefetch is admin-only so we recommend the SDK for most users.

docs-bot: PR 4683 updated  requested reviewers: carla, jia, maya.

jia: small suggestion on wording: avoid 'instant' speedups. prefer 'reduced cold-start latency' and show token/sec deltas.

maya: I fixed the console link in the doc to /console/optimize/kv-prefetch and left a redirect note for older links. Also added the perf table (very small):
- batch=1 seq=512: 12 tok/s
- batch=4 seq=512: 33 tok/s
- batch=4 seq=2048: 22 tok/s
(marked example-only)

ada: also added a short migration checklist for internal release notes: 
- update examples repo path
- publish migration doc link in Optimize Toolkit index
- notify Support about the admin-hosted prefetch caveat

ryan: reviewing now. one nit: mention that prefetch_kv accepts TTL and a best-practice value (e.g., 1h) for dynamic content.

carla: LGTM from copy side pending jia's kernel wording review. If all green I'll approve and merge later today.

ben: :thumbsup: Will follow up with a tiny runtime RFC if we need extra telemetry for prefetch hit rates.

ada: Great team. After merge I'll open a quick tweet-thread draft and a support KB note.
